Someone died in this Chengdu flat. Ninety-two people fought to buy it anyway.
Eighty-nine square meters, fully finished, near the subway. Worth about one point six million yuan.
But it's listed as the scene of an unnatural death. In China, that makes it a haunted house, and buyers stay away.
So in November twenty twenty-five, a court put it up for auction, starting at just two hundred and sixty-six thousand yuan.
Ninety-two people signed up to bid.
In the final minutes, the bids kept coming. The clock reset fourteen times.
Final price: one point zero five six million yuan. Almost four times the starting price.
Then the winner put it straight back up for auction.
January. Someone bid nine hundred and sixty-six thousand, couldn't pay, and lost a fifty thousand yuan deposit.
April. Third auction. Starting price: one hundred and sixty-six thousand.
It sold for nine hundred and eighty-six thousand. The November buyer lost about seventy thousand yuan.
What happened inside was never made public. The bidders didn't seem to care.
